Alert.description:
One lifecycle event of an operator-facing alert (bus topic ``alerts``, ADR 0011).

Alarm states follow ISA-18.2: ``active`` (the condition is present) and ``acknowledged``
(an operator has seen it) are independent. Every transition (raise, clear, acknowledge,
re-raise) is a new append-only event with the same ``alertId`` and the next ``rev``; the
current alert is the event with the highest ``rev``. An alert is resolved (no longer shown)
once it is both cleared and acknowledged.

``ts`` is on the event-time axis (ADR 0010); ``ackedAt`` is the wall-clock time of the
acknowledgement. ``kind`` is a short machine-readable code (e.g. ``machine_fault``),
``source`` names the producer (e.g. ``engine``).
Alert.title: Alert

One telemetry sample from one machine.

Sensor values are nullable: ``null`` (or an absent key) means the sensor value is missing
for this sample. The ingest pipeline keeps partially missing readings with
``quality=SUSPECT`` and quarantines readings without any sensor value (ADR 0007).

ScenarioRequest.description:
A simulation-only request to inject a fault or load a scenario (ADR 0015).

Stored in the event store (stream ``scenario_requests``) so injected faults can be told
apart from real ones in replay and experiments. ``ts`` is on the event-time axis (the
source's watermark when the request was made). ``faultType`` names a simulator fault
(e.g. ``bearing_wear``); the simulator validates it.
ScenarioRequest.title: ScenarioRequest

info.description:
LineTwin backend: live state of the production-line twin, event-store queries, alerts,
operator commands, source management and (simulation only) scenario injection.

**Auth:** send an API key in the `X-API-Key` header. Viewers can read; operators can also send
commands, switch sources and acknowledge alerts. Without configured keys the server serves
read-only access on a loopback address only. WebSocket clients authenticate with their first
message (see the WebSocket reference in docs/api.md).
info.title: LineTwin API
